utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Defence had a short preliminary matter -- the Prosecution, yes. I'm looking at the Prosecution. That the Prosecution wanted to raise a matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It will be very brief so I think the witness could even be brought in but first ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few other things before the witness can be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think will be best addressed once we've gone into closed session for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait for that. What I'd like to do is first to deliver two decisions on behalf of the Chamber. The first one is -- the Chamber will deal with the Defence notice, objection and motion to bar Witness Riedlmayer from testifying as an expert which was filed on the 7th of June, 2013. The Prosecution responded to the motion on the 18th of June, 2013. With regard to the applicable law concerning expert evidence, the Chamber refers to its decision concerning Richard Butler, filed on the 19th of October, 2012. With regard to Riedlmayer's expertise, the Defence submits that Riedlmayer should be disqualified as an expert and the Prosecution should be barred from presenting his evidence. However, both parties acknowledge that Riedlmayer is an expert and the matter in dispute is limited to the exact scope of his expertise and whether his report goes beyond that scope. The Chamber is satisfied that Riedlmayer is an expert who can assist the Chamber on matters related to the destruction of cultural monuments in Bosnia-Herzegovina. As for the exact scope of Riedlmayer's expertise, the Chamber considers that this can be explored during the examination of the witness in court. Similarly, as for any arguments related to the content and methodology of the Riedlmayer report, the Chamber considers that such matters should be addressed during the examination of the witness. The Chamber defers its decision on admission of the report to the time of the witness's testimony. With regard to the Defence request to cross-examine the witness, the Chamber notes that he will be called to testify and the Defence will therefore have the opportunity to cross-examine him. Based on the foregoing, the Chamber decides that Witness Riedlmayer may testify as an expert witness and denies the Defence request to bar the Prosecution from presenting his evidence. This concludes the Chamber's decision on the Defence notice, objection, and motion to bar Witness Riedlmayer from testifying. Next decision I'll deliver is a decision on the Prosecution's 24th emotion to admit evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis. This decision will be delivered orally. That is not the new practice of the Chamber so therefore it is exceptional. The Chamber, as I said, will now deliver its decision on the Prosecution's 24th Rule 92 bis motion, filed on the 3rd of April, 2013. In its motion, the Prosecution tendered the evidence of five witnesses. The Defence responded on the 16th of July, 2013, opposing the motion in relation to four witnesses. On the 22nd of July, the Prosecution requested leave to reply to the response and submitted a more legible version of one of the tendered statements. Considering that the motion covers five witnesses, the Chamber grants the Prosecution's request to exceed the word limit in its motion. The Chamber is further satisfied that it is assisted by the reply and therefore grants the requested leave to reply. The Chamber refers to the parties' filings for their submissions and the Chamber's previous Rule 92 bis decision of the 19th of October, 2012, for the applicable law. The Chamber will now analyse whether the proffered documents meet the requirements of Rule 89(C) and 92 bis. First, having reviewed the proffered documents, the Chamber considers them to relate, inter alia, to alleged sniping and shelling incidents in Sarajevo as well as to alleged ethnic violence in Grbavica in 1992. As you such, the Chamber is satisfied as to the evidence's relevance vis-a-vis the indictment. The Chamber further considers that the statements appear to be internally consistent. The Defence's objections that two witnesses provide speculative testimony relate to small parts of the evidence; hence, do not affect the documents' probative value to such an extent as to require exclusion or that the witnesses be called for cross-examination. The Defence's submission as to inconsistencies in Witness Beslic's evidence goes to the weight to be given to the evidence at a later stage. Accordingly, the Chamber finds that the proffered evidence is of probative value as required under Rule 89(C). No, I said -- yes, 89(C). Second, the Chamber notes that the proffered documents do not concern the acts and conduct of the accused. Third, the statements of the witnesses are either accompanied by the required attestation pursuant to Rule 92 bis (B) or were attested to by the witnesses in prior Tribunal proceedings. Fourth, the proffered documents are of a cumulative nature with respect to the evidence of witnesses who have already testified before the Chamber, as well as generally consistent with adjudicated facts of which this Chamber has taken judicial notice. The proffered evidence concerns crime-base evidence. Fifth, in relation to the associated exhibits tendered in the motion, the Chamber is satisfied that as the documents were discussed by the witnesses in their written evidence to such an extent that their non-admission would decrease the probative value of the written evidence, they form an inseparable and indispensable part of the statements or transcripts to which they are associated. The Chamber is further unconvinced by the Defence submission that Witness Zaimovic's notes are in essence unofficial medical records which require cross-examination to test their reliability. The point raised by the Defence, again, related to the weight to be given to the evidence and not its admissibility. Lastly, the Chamber notes that some portions of Witness Hajir's statement are very general conclusions by the witness that do not assist the Chamber. As such, the Chamber decides that these portions, namely paragraphs 14 and 59, should be redacted. For these reasons, the Chamber finds that the proffered evidence is admissible pursuant to Rule 92 bis. The Prosecution has tendered limited portions of the transcripts from previous cases, which supplement the evidence in the witness statements. The Chamber finds that the tendering of this transcript evidence complies with the Chamber's guidance on this matter. Accordingly, the Chamber grants the motion and admits the following into evidence: For Witness Beslic: The statement of the 30th of January, 2007, and related attestation, as well as the excerpts of his testimony in the Dragomir Milosevic case as specified in Annex A of the motion. For Witness Gavrankapetanovic: The statements of 11 of October, 2001, 13 December 2001, and 17th January, 2002, plus the related attestations, as well as the excerpts of his testimony in the Galic case and the three associated exhibits, all specified in Annex A to the motion. For Witness Hajir: The redacted statement of 25 February 2010, plus the table of concordance, as well as the excerpts of his testimony in the Karadzic case and the three associated exhibits, all specified in Annex A of the motion. For Witness Zaimovic: The statement of the 26th of February, 2010, as well as the excerpts of her testimony in the Karadzic case and the two associated exhibits, all specified in Annex A of the motion. For witness RM141: The statement of 5 February 2011, as well as the excerpts of the witness's testimony in the Karadzic case and the two associated exhibits, all specified in Annex C of the motion. The statement and the first associated exhibit listed in Annex C are admitted under seal. The Registry is hereby requested to assign numbers to the documents admitted into evidence and inform the parties and the Chamber of the numbers so assigned. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. For the testimony of the next witness, we move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Madam Registrar informs me that the number P2367, which was just assigned to 65 ter number 02839, that we don't need that number because that -- this same document has already been admitted into evidence under number P2443. Therefore, the number can be -- the number 2 -- no. I'm now making a mistake. 65 ter number 02839, which was assigned P2443 today, there is no need to admit it twice because the same document is already in evidence as P2367, and therefore P2443 is vacated. I'll try to be as quick as possible. First, I put on the record that the Chamber earlier this morning delivered a decision in closed session in which leave was granted to add a document, document 65 ter 30316, to the Prosecution's exhibit list. Then next item. On the 26th of April of this year, the Prosecution sought to add 23 documents to its Rule 65 ter exhibit list. The documents relate to Witness Andras Riedlmayer. Having reviewed the documents and in light of the fact that the Defence had not opposed the Prosecution's request, the Chamber finds that it's in the interest of justice to have them added and therefore grants leave to add them to the Rule 65 ter list. Last item as far as I am concerned: Decision on Defence request for an extension of time to respond. On the 1st of October, 2013, the Defence filed a request for an extension of 30 days in which to respond to the Prosecution's 38th 92 bis motion, citing the length of the proffered witness statement. The Chamber notes the Prosecution's standing submission that it will not object to any reasonable requests for extensions. The Chamber grants an additional 30 days in which to respond setting the new dead-line of the 31st of October, 2013. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. All other matters which are on my list are not urgent and therefore I'll not further test your patience. We have a non-sitting week next week. We will not sit tomorrow. We therefore adjourn until Wednesday, the 16th of October, 2013, at 9.30 in the morning in courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of October, 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
